reason: DoS via unbounded brace expansion, in a BUILD-TIME glob matcher only. The advisory has no back-ported fix (single range, fixed: 5.0.8) and brace-expansion@5 changed its export from a function to an object, so forcing it breaks minimatch@3 — which eslint itself depends on (eslint -> minimatch@^3.1.2). We tried that in #297 and it silently broke every `eslint` invocation using a brace glob. brace-expansion is never shipped to the browser and only ever expands glob patterns we author ourselves, so there is no untrusted input path. Revisit when eslint moves off minimatch@3 (or when the ESLint-CLI migration lands, whichever comes first).
